noteRef.topicTitle: 1. Structure, Bonding & Introduction to Organic Chemistry

specPoints.text: be able to draw and name the structural isomers of alkanes and cycloalkanes with up to six carbon atoms

primer.text: One molecular formula can build several real compounds: structural isomers wire the same atoms differently. Branching shortens the longest chain (pentane against 2,2-dimethylpropane); moving a functional group re-addresses it (butan-1-ol against butan-2-ol); and a hunt protocol - draw, decide stereo or structural, classify - counts them all, from four dibromopropanes to two C4H10 skeletons.

lessons.title: Same formula, different molecule
lessons.opening: Structural isomers are compounds with one molecular formula but different structural formulae: same atoms, wired differently. Propene and cyclopropane both count three carbons and six hydrogens, yet one is an open alkene and the other a ring. The two flavours of structural isomerism to master are chain isomerism and positional isomerism.
keyPoints: Structural isomers share the same molecular formula but differ in structural formulae.
Propene and cyclopropane are isomers - both C3H6, one open-chained, one ringed.
Chain isomerism arises when the longest hydrocarbon chain differs.
Positional isomerism arises when the same functional group sits on different carbons.
Counting atoms never separates isomers - only the bonding arrangement does.

low.restatement: Same ingredient list, different assembly: isomers fool the formula but not the structure.
low.analogy: The same LEGO bricks built as a tower or an arch - identical inventory, different model.
low.examPointer: Always demonstrate isomerism by writing both structural formulae - the difference is the proof.

medium.restatement: Isomerism is a connectivity distinction: identical molecular formulae with different bonding arrangements, classified by WHAT differs - the skeleton (chain) or the functional group's address (positional) - while the atom inventory stays fixed.
medium.analogy: Two routes on one map between the same towns: identical endpoints (formula), different roads taken (structure).
medium.examPointer: Propene versus cyclopropane is the canonical demo pair - quote both C3H6 formulae and their differing structures.

check.stem: What do structural isomers share?

options.explanation: That would make them the same compound.

check.stem: What differs between structural isomers?

options.text: Their structural formulae - the bonding arrangement

check.stem: Propene and cyclopropane are structural isomers because

options.text: both are made of 3 carbons and 6 hydrogens but joined differently - one open chain, one ring

options.explanation: Their structures differ - that is the point.

check.stem: Which two types of structural isomerism does the syllabus require?

options.explanation: Functional-group isomerism is not in this pair.

check.stem: Two compounds share a molecular formula but differ in every property list. What explains this?

options.text: Different structural formulae give different substances with different properties

check.stem: Define structural isomers.
check.modelAnswer: Structural isomers are separate compounds wearing one identical molecular formula while their structural formulae diverge.

check.stem: Name the two structural isomerism types required at this level.
Explain why identical molecular formulae can still describe different compounds.
check.modelAnswer: A molecular formula only inventories atoms; how those atoms connect - which bond links which atom - is extra information, and different connectivities are genuinely different substances.

check.stem: A student lists two structures, both C3H6, one with a C=C and one as a triangle ring. State the isomer relationship and the differing feature.
check.modelAnswer: They are structural isomers - propene and cyclopropane - sharing the C3H6 molecular formula while differing in structure: open chain versus ring.

lessons.title: Chain isomerism: the branching disease
lessons.opening: Chain isomerism keeps the molecular formula and changes the longest hydrocarbon chain - branching is the cause. Pentane's straight five-carbon chain and 2,2-dimethylpropane's three-carbon backbone with two methyl branches hold identical atom inventories yet name different longest chains: five versus three.
keyPoints: Chain isomerism means same molecular formula but different longest hydrocarbon chain.
Pentane and 2,2-dimethylpropane are chain isomers of the same formula.
Pentane's longest chain runs five carbons; 2,2-dimethylpropane's runs three, with two methyl branches.
The atom inventory is unchanged - only the chain architecture differs.

low.restatement: Same atoms, different skeleton: branch the chain and the longest run shortens, giving a chain isomer.
low.analogy: The same rope re-knotted: straight it spans five marks; knotted mid-way its longest straight run is three.
low.examPointer: State both longest-chain lengths when demonstrating chain isomerism - the numbers are the evidence.

medium.restatement: Chain isomerism relocates carbons from the main chain into branches: the molecular formula is conserved while the maximum contiguous run of carbons contracts, which is why pentane (C5 chain) and 2,2-dimethylpropane (C3 chain plus two methyls) qualify.
medium.analogy: A motorway re-routed through side streets: same total tarmac, shorter longest straight stretch.
medium.examPointer: 'Caused by branching' is the quotable cause - pair it with the longest-chain contrast.

check.stem: What stays the same in chain isomerism?
What causes chain isomerism?
How long is the longest chain in 2,2-dimethylpropane?

options.text: Three carbons, with two methyl branches
options.explanation: The quaternary centre caps a three-carbon run.
The branches are methyls on carbon 2.

check.stem: Pentane and 2,2-dimethylpropane are chain isomers because

options.text: they share the same molecular formula but their longest chains run 5 and 3 carbons respectively

check.stem: A compound's longest chain is five carbons; its isomer's is three with two methyl branches. The molecular formulae are

options.explanation: That is a homologous-step difference, not isomers.
They are the same formula by definition.

check.stem: Define chain isomerism.
check.modelAnswer: Chain isomerism keeps a shared molecular formula while the longest hydrocarbon chain changes length - branching is the cause.

check.stem: State the longest-chain lengths of pentane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.
check.modelAnswer: Pentane's longest chain is 5; 2,2-dimethylpropane's is 3, carrying two methyl branches.

check.stem: Explain why branching shortens the longest chain without changing the molecular formula.
check.modelAnswer: Branching moves carbons off the main run into side pieces: the total carbon count is untouched, but the longest contiguous sequence of bonded carbons shrinks, and that sequence is what the name counts.

check.stem: A student draws C5H12 as a straight chain and then as a three-carbon chain with two methyl branches. Name the relationship and the isomerism type.
check.modelAnswer: The two drawings are structural isomers - pentane and 2,2-dimethylpropane - related by chain isomerism, since branching shortened the longest chain from 5 to 3.

lessons.title: Positional isomerism and the isomer hunt
lessons.opening: Positional isomers carry the same functional group on different carbons: butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol both hold four carbons, ten hydrogens and one oxygen - only the -OH's address moves. The hunting protocol then generalises: draw the structure, decide structural versus stereo, and walk the checklist - functional group? chain? positional? Dibromopropane yields four positional isomers; C4H10 yields two chain isomers.
keyPoints: Positional isomers differ in the position of the same functional group.
Butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol both hold 4 carbons, 10 hydrogens and one oxygen - the OH moves from carbon 1 to carbon 2.
The hunt protocol: draw the structure, decide structural versus stereo, then check functional group, chain, positional in turn.
Dibromopropane, C3H6Br2, shows positional isomerism - the two bromines sit on different carbons - yielding 4 isomers.
C4H10 shows chain isomerism only, yielding 2 isomers: butane and 2-methylpropane.

low.restatement: Same group, different address: slide the functional group along the chain and each stop is a positional isomer. To hunt all isomers, draw, decide the type, then walk the checklist.
low.analogy: The same shop sign hung on different doors of one street - same shop, different address.
low.examPointer: Quote the atom inventory when demonstrating positional isomers - C4H10O for both butanols - then point at the differing carbon.

medium.restatement: The positional mechanism relocates a functional group across equivalent-or-not carbons while conserving the formula; the hunt protocol then enumerates systematically - restricted rotation splits stereo from structural, and the functional-group/chain/positional checklist classifies each structural case, as dibromopropane's four bromine placements and C4H10's two skeletons show.
medium.analogy: A building survey: first decide whether differences are architectural (structural) or mirror-image (stereo), then audit each floor - group placement, skeleton shape, group address.
medium.examPointer: Walk the checklist in order and answer each step explicitly - marks attach to the reasoning, not just the count.

check.stem: What defines positional isomers?

options.text: The same functional group located on different carbon atoms

check.stem: Butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol differ in

options.text: which carbon carries the OH group - first versus second

check.stem: Why does dibromopropane show positional rather than chain isomerism?

options.text: The longest chain can only run three carbons, but the two bromines can occupy different carbons
options.explanation: Placement varies where the skeleton cannot.

options.text: Its bromines can leave the molecule
options.explanation: The formula is fixed at C3H6Br2.
The protocol found none, so it is structural.

options.text: It carries two functional group types
options.explanation: Br is the only functional group possible.

check.stem: How many positional isomers does dibromopropane, C3H6Br2, have?

options.explanation: The distinct bromine placements on a three-carbon chain.

check.stem: How many isomers does C4H10 have, and of which type?

options.text: Two, both chain isomers - butane and 2-methylpropane
options.explanation: No functional group exists to reposition.
Only two skeletons exist for four carbons.

check.stem: Define positional isomerism.
check.modelAnswer: Positional isomerism relocates one unchanged functional group: it takes up residence on different carbons across the isomers.

check.stem: State the three steps of the isomer-hunting protocol.
check.modelAnswer: Draw the structural formula; determine whether it is stereo or structural isomerism; determine whether it is functional group, chain or positional.

check.stem: Explain why C4H10 shows chain isomerism but no positional isomerism.
check.modelAnswer: With no functional groups present, nothing can move position between carbons; the only variation available is the carbon skeleton, so branching produces the two chain isomers.

check.stem: Run the protocol on C3H6Br2 and list the positional placements that give the four isomers.
check.modelAnswer: Structural (no restricted rotation); no functional-group type (Br only), no chain type (chain capped at 3); positional - the placements 1,1-, 1,2-, 1,3- and 2,2-dibromopropane give four isomers.

glossary.definition: One of a set of compounds sharing a molecular formula but differing in structural formula.
Isomerism where the longest hydrocarbon chain differs because of branching.
Isomerism where the same functional group occupies different carbon positions.

workedExample.prompt: How many isomers does dibromopropane, C3H6Br2, have?
steps: Draw the structure: a three-carbon chain bearing two bromines.
No restricted rotation about the C-C bond, so the isomerism is structural.
Functional-group type? No - bromine is the only group available here. Chain type? No - the longest run stops at three carbons. Positional type? Yes - the two bromines can take up different carbons.
The placements 1,1-, 1,2-, 1,3- and 2,2-dibromopropane give four isomers.
